extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors preparing/submitting journal manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on common reasons manuscripts are desk-rejected and concrete steps to improve a research paper prior to journal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk rejection (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A desk reject, also known as a desk rejection, is when your paper is turned down by a journal, prior to them sending it out for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This type of rejection can feel disappointing; to avoid it, know the journal’s expectations and follow the other recommendations on the page (scope, format, novelty, methodology, language, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your journal and follow its guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication will have standards and expectations that you can review prior to submitting your manuscript. Before you send it in for consideration, make sure you are following the journal’s guidelines, to the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the journal’s aims/scope and published papers to understand what they publish; strict adherence to submission instructions reduces likelihood of desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation / statement of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovate: When a research study is innovative in its approach, it has a much more likely chance of being accepted by a scientific journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a 'statement of novelty' in the introduction and, if appropriate, mention the innovation within the abstract and conclusion. Study other papers published by the journal and in your field to help write your statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plagiarism (including self-plagiarism)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’ve copied the work, deliberately or otherwise, of other researchers, you may be accused of plagiarism. You can also be called out if you, effectively, plagiarize your own work by simply repackaging it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications run manuscripts through plagiarism-detection software. If a manuscript shows a duplication of around 20%, the manuscript will be returned for edits; if much higher, publishers may report the manuscript as plagiarized. Ensure proper citation, paraphrase correctly, and avoid repackaging prior work without disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope / journal fit (including regional fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate scope: understand the journal and if your research fits into what the journal wants to publish. A journal’s scope may also be 'regional.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond scientific topic fit, check whether the journal expects regional relevance or other topical boundaries. Submitting to a journal without fit increases chance of desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet required publication format
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep to the format that the journal requests; format noncompliance can compound other shortfalls identified by editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although format alone may not be the sole reason for rejection, following the journal’s formatting and submission rules removes an avoidable barrier. Note editors may reject a large proportion of submissions (the article cites editors reject up to 70% of manuscripts), so removing small faults helps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript quality: structure, completeness, and broader impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellent manuscript quality: the manuscript must include sections that are standard to the journal type—for instance, an introduction, materials and methodology, research results, a discussion section, and the conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond presenting specific results and conclusions, manuscripts should address how research may be applied to a more general purpose and discuss broader impacts and implications of findings. Ensure logical flow, completeness of standard sections, and clear exposition of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellent methodology (rigor and justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the methodology used in the research is sub-par, the manuscript may be rejected outright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid simplistic or under-specified methods, ensure important details are considered, and justify chosen methods within the context of more established approaches. Demonstrate rigor, appropriateness, and reproducibility of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper grammar and English usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals are international, and the expected language for submission of a manuscript is English. It is not uncommon for a manuscript to be rejected because the English used is not up to par for a highly regarded international journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a native English speaker who is familiar with the topic review and edit your document. Consider professional language-editing services to ensure spelling, grammar, and usage do not distract from the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong abstract and cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t think of your abstract and cover letter as a quick, last-minute thing to attach to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong, convincing cover letter can get attention from editorial staff. The abstract should highlight innovation, outstanding methodology, findings, and implications clearly to make the argument for publication. Prepare these carefully to improve chances of being sent for peer review.
